thread:
Maria O.: hey all — getting multiple escalations from Support: hosted API returning 5xx and timeouts for a bunch of EU customers, starting ~03:12 UTC. sample errors attached by customers. can we triage? :rotating_light:

Katie - Support: customers reporting spikes of 502/504, many are paying enterprise tenants. ticket IDs: #2248, #2252. They're seeing timeouts for long running chat streams and also short text gen calls.

Samir (oncall): looking. graph of 5xx shows a sharp jump at 03:10, peaked 03:14. Correlated with auth proxy error rate.

Trent - Runtime: gateway logs show upstream status 502 from auth-verify service, not model backend. load on EU gateway normal, but auth-verify CPU lat spiking + retries.

Ivy - Auth: we rotated the KMS key for signed tokens at 03:00 per schedule. I'm pulling logs now.

Katie - Support: customers angry, two threads escalating to CSM. can we give ETA for mitigation?

Samir (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) route EU traffic to fallback auth verifier (non-KMS path) for 15m; 2) enable circuit breaker on gateway to avoid retry storm; 3) page Trent/runtime to increase auth verifier replicas. doing step 1 now.

Trent - Runtime: scaling auth-verify from 4 -> 12 in eu-west. taking ~90s to add pods. enabling breaker policy to short-circuit after 3 upstream failures.

deploy-bot: started rolling change: auth-verify-fallback-route -> ENABLED in eu-west by Samir (oncall) at 03:22 UTC

Samir (oncall): fallback routing is active. monitoring errors.

Ivy - Auth: confirmed: KMS rotation produced a short window where token validator attempted to use new key but some signing services were still issuing tokens with old thumbprint; that mismatch produced verification errors which the auth-verify service surfaced as 502 when it attempted to fetch key metadata. We should have returned 401 for invalid token instead of 502.

Maria O.: ok. can we produce repro steps so support can follow? Katie can paste customer repro below if available.

Katie - Support: pasted a repro curl:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <legacy-sub-token>" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response from affected time: 502 with body: "upstream verify: key fetch failed: 500 - metadata timeout"

Samir (oncall): I can reproduce locally hitting eu gateway with an old token — getting 502 from auth-verify. logs: ``[auth-verify] key_lookup failed: timeout fetching key metadata (KMS 503) -> categorized as upstream error``

Trent - Runtime: because auth-verify responded with 502 the gateway retried requests to model pool which amplified load. adding short-term rate limit on retries and disabling automatic retry for auth-related failures.

Ivy - Auth: live fix: deploy small patch to auth-verify to classify key fetch issues as transient and return 401/429 to callers instead of 502. will deploy to eu-west canary now.

deploy-bot: deploying auth-verify fix to eu-west-canary by Ivy at 03:30 UTC

Samir (oncall): canary looks good, retest with legacy token — now gateway returns 401 instead of 502. Rolling to remainder of eu-west.

deploy-bot: rollout complete to eu-west by Ivy at 03:34 UTC

Maria O.: errors falling from 18% -> 1.4% within 5 minutes. customer reports coming in: a few transient failures but most recovered. :white_check_mark:

Katie - Support: sending proactive note to impacted customers explaining transient key rotation mismatch and that we routed to fallback and rolled a fix; offering credit for downtime window 03:10-03:35 UTC.

Samir (oncall): current status: mitigated. moving to postmortem. notes so far: root cause = KMS key rotation race between token issuance and validator lookup, plus auth-verify returning 502 which triggered gateway retries and increased load.

Ivy - Auth: action items I propose: 1) add a tolerant validation window during key rotations (accept both keys for 10m), 2) ensure auth-verify maps key fetch failures -> 401/429 not 502, 3) add KMS rotation canary.

Trent - Runtime: runtime action items: 1) default gateway retry policy: do not retry when upstream failure is from auth path, 2) improve retry budget metrics and alarm (we hit retry storm), 3) add per-route circuit breaker to stop cascading retries.

Maria O.: support/process items: 1) update incident runbook to include KMS rotation checklist (notify support & SRE), 2) automation to open an incident channel on rotation if key churn > threshold, 3) billing/CS follow-up email template.

Samir (oncall): quick postmortem timeline to capture: 03:00 KMS rotation, 03:10 spike begins, 03:22 fallback routing, 03:30 fix deployed, 03:34 rollback complete, 03:35 errors back to baseline.

Katie - Support: I will draft customer communication and attach sample repros and safe-mitigation steps.

Ivy - Auth: will follow up with PRs for tolerant validation + canary within 48h.

Trent - Runtime: will create a short RFC for retry policy update and implement circuit breaker config within 72h.

Maria O.: assigning owners: Ivy -> auth fixes + KMS canary, Trent -> gateway retry/circuit updates, Samir -> postmortem doc and incident timeline, Katie -> customer comms + credits. Please add tasks to the incident board.

incidents-bot: action items recorded: #INC-2050001111-1 (Ivy), #INC-2050001111-2 (Trent), #INC-2050001111-3 (Samir), #INC-2050001111-4 (Katie)

Samir (oncall): final note — short term we should avoid scheduled KMS rotations during EU maintenance window until we have canary. Logging is the hero here: add a header trace for KMS key thumbprint on every token so we can correlate quickly next time.

Maria O.: thanks everyone. if anything else pops up, ping here. I'll kick off the postmortem doc now. :spiral_note_pad:
